issue: Does 'controlled substance' in U.S.S.G. § 4B1.2(b) (the career offender guideline) refer to the federal Controlled Substances Act definition, or can it include a state drug offense that criminalizes substances the federal government does not control?

sides.position: 'Controlled substance' in § 4B1.2(b) refers to the federal definition, so a state drug conviction counts as a predicate only if the substance is also federally controlled (the Jerome presumption favors federal law).
cases: United States v. Townsend, 897 F.3d 66 (2d Cir. 2018)
United States v. Leal-Vega, 680 F.3d 1160 (9th Cir. 2012)
United States v. Pittman, 736 F. App'x 551 (6th Cir. 2018)
United States v. Ruth, No. 20-1034 (7th Cir. 2020)

sides.position: 'Controlled substance' in § 4B1.2(b) is not limited to federally controlled substances, so a state conviction for dealing a substance the state controls can qualify as a predicate offense.
cases: United States v. Whitfield, 726 F. App'x 373 (6th Cir. 2018)
United States v. Sheffey, 2020 WL 3495944 (6th Cir. June 29, 2020)
United States v. Ruth, No. 20-1034 (7th Cir. 2020)

quote: We recognize that a circuit split exists on this issue, and that the weight of authority favors Ruth.
cite: United States v. Nathaniel Ruth, No. 20-1034 (7th Cir. 2020)
